name: Cap Polyposis

criteria.description: Presence of multiple inflammatory polyps with characteristic 'cap' of granulation tissue on colonoscopy
Histological confirmation of polyps showing fibrinopurulent exudate (cap) overlying elongated, tortuous crypts
Chronic mucoid and bloody diarrhea with abdominal pain
Exclusion of other polyposis syndromes and inflammatory bowel disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic inflammatory polyps with cap on histology plus compatible clinical symptoms and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on endoscopic and histopathologic findings combined with clinical presentation.

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) in some cases
imaging: Colonoscopy showing multiple sessile polyps with characteristic caps
Barium enema may show multiple polypoid lesions in rectosigmoid colon
genetic: No known genetic mutations associated; sporadic cases
other: Histopathology demonstrating inflammatory polyps with fibrinopurulent cap and elongated crypts

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of hamartomatous juvenile polyps without fibrinopurulent cap
Genetic mutations in SMAD4 or BMPR1A
Histology shows crypt abscesses and chronic inflammatory infiltrate
Systemic symptoms and extraintestinal manifestations more common
Polypoid lesions related to mucosal prolapse without characteristic cap
Associated with chronic straining and rectal prolapse

redFlags: Severe rectal bleeding causing hemodynamic instability
Rapid increase in polyp size or number
Signs of bowel obstruction or intussusception
references: Kusunoki M, et al. Cap polyposis: clinical features and treatment outcomes. World J Gastroenterol. 2015.
Matsumoto T, et al. Histopathological characteristics of cap polyposis. J Gastroenterol Hepatol. 2010.
